newsitem.title: USA: Other visitors slew executive's son - teen suspect.
newsitem.headline: Other visitors slew executive's son - teen suspect.

text.p: A teenager accused of killing the son of Time Warner chairman Gerald Levin said in court papers released Monday that two other men committed the murder and he had just been taking drugs with the victim.
Corey Arthur, 19, is charged with the murder of Jonathan Levin in his Manhattan apartment May 30. Levin's body was found two days later.

Police believe that Levin was tortured by Arthur and his co-defendant, Mantoun Hart, 25, with a steak knife until he revealed his personal bank code number. Arthur and Hart then withdrew $800 from Levin's account, police say.
Levin, 31, was an English teacher at New York's Taft High School.
Arthur, who police believe was the gunman in the slaying, pleaded not guilty to murder and robbery charges at his arraignment Monday in Manhattan State Supreme Court. Hart also has pleaded innocent.
In a seven-page confession police say Arthur made to detectives, Arthur recalled going to Levin's apartment because Levin had contacted him and asked him to bring "lots of drugs."
He said they had smoked crack at the apartment.
While Arthur was there, he continued, Levin let two unidentified men inside, one of whom ordered Arthur to bind Levin with duct tape, which he did.
Then one man cut Arthur with a knife and Arthur fled, afraid to call the police, he said.
Detectives said Arthur told them at the time of his arrest: "I didn't want to become famous like this. I was just trying to make some money. He was my friend too, you know."
